et apertum est os meum et non est clausum amplius.
Altissimus autem dedit intellectum quinque viris, et scripserunt quae dicebantur ex successione notis quas non sciebant, et sederunt quadraginta diebus. Ipsi autem per diem scribebant,
nocte autem manducabant panem; ego autem per diem loquebar et nocte non tacebam.
Scripti sunt autem in quadraginta diebus libri nongenti quattuor.
Et factum est cum conpleti essent quadraginta dies, et locutus est Altissimus dicens: Priora quae scripsisti in palam pone, et legant digni et indigni.
Novissimos autem septuaginta conservabis, ut tradas eos sapientibus de populo tuo.
In his enim est vena intellectus et sapientiae fons et scientiae flumen. Et feci sic.

unit.reading: In the thirtieth year after the ruin of the city, I, Salathiel, who am also Ezra, was in Babylon; and I was troubled as I lay upon my bed, and my thoughts mounted up into my heart,
because I saw the desolation of Zion and the abundance of those who dwelt in Babylon.
And my spirit was greatly agitated, and I began to speak fear-filled words to the Most High,
and said: "O Sovereign Lord, did you not speak at the beginning, when you—and you alone—fashioned the earth and commanded the dust,
and it gave Adam a dead body? Yet it was also the workmanship of your hands, and you breathed into him the breath of life, and he became alive before you.
And you led him into paradise, which your right hand had planted before the earth appeared.

And to him you gave a single commandment of yours, but he transgressed it, and immediately you appointed death for him and for his generations. And from him were born nations and tribes, peoples and clans, of which there is no number.
And each nation walked according to its own will, and they acted impiously before you and despised your commandments, and you did not restrain them.
Then again, in due time, you brought the flood upon the inhabitants of the world and destroyed them.
And the same lot befell them: as death was to Adam, so was the flood to these.
Yet you left one of them, Noah with his household, and from him came all the righteous.
And it came to pass, when those who dwelt upon the earth began to multiply, and produced children and peoples and many nations, they began again to commit impiety more than their predecessors.
And it came to pass, when they were committing iniquity before you, you chose for yourself one from among them, whose name was Abraham.
And you loved him, and to him alone, secretly by night, you revealed the end of the times.
And you established an everlasting covenant with him, and promised him that you would never forsake his descendants. And you gave him Isaac, and to Isaac you gave Jacob and Esau.
And you set Jacob apart for yourself, but Esau you separated; and Jacob became a great multitude.
And it came to pass, when you brought his descendants out of Egypt, you led them to Mount Sinai.
You bent the heavens and shook the earth, and stirred the world, and made the depths tremble, and troubled the age.
And your glory passed through four gates—of fire, earthquake, wind, and frost—to give the law to the descendants of Jacob and the commandment to the generation of Israel.
Yet you did not take away from them the evil heart, so that your law might bear fruit in them.
For the first Adam, bearing an evil heart, transgressed and was overcome, as were all who were born from him.
And permanent infirmity was established: the law was in the heart of the people along with the evil root; so what was good departed, and the evil remained.
And times passed and the years were completed, and you raised up for yourself a servant named David.
And you told him to build a city for your name, and to offer to you in it oblations from what is yours.
And this was done for many years. But the inhabitants of the city went astray,
doing in all things just as Adam and all his generations had done; for they also possessed an evil heart.
And so you handed over your city into the hands of your enemies.
Then I said in my heart: 'Do those who inhabit Babylon do any better, and is it on this account that she rules over Zion?'
For it came to pass, when I came here, that I saw impieties without number, and my soul has seen many transgressors in this thirtieth year. And my heart failed,
because I saw how you endure those who sin and have spared those who act impiously, and have destroyed your people and preserved your enemies, and have not indicated
anything to anyone as to how this way ought to be forsaken. Does Babylon act better than Zion,
or has any other nation known you except Israel? Or what tribes have believed your covenants as these of Jacob have,
whose reward has not appeared, nor has their labor borne fruit? For I have traveled through the nations, and I have seen them flourishing and unmindful of your commandments.
Now therefore weigh our iniquities and those of the inhabitants of the world in the balance, and it will be found where the scale turns.
Or when have the inhabitants of the earth not sinned in your sight? Or what nation has kept your commandments in such a way?
You will indeed find individual persons by name who have kept your commandments, but nations you will not find.
And the angel who had been sent to me, whose name was Uriel, answered me
and said to me: "Your understanding has utterly failed regarding this age, and do you think you can comprehend the way of the Most High?"
And I said: "Yes, my lord." And he answered me and said: "I have been sent to show you three ways, and to set three parables before you.
If you can declare one of these to me, I also will show you the way you desire to see, and I will teach you why the heart is evil."
And I said: "Speak, my lord." And he said to me: "Go, weigh for me the weight of fire, or measure for me the blast of the wind, or recall for me the day that has passed."
And I answered and said: "Who among mortals can do this, that you should ask me about these things?"

And he said to me: "If I had asked you, saying: 'How many dwellings are in the heart of the sea, or how many springs are at the beginning of the deep, or how many streams are above the firmament, or what are the exits of paradise?'
perhaps you would have said to me: 'I have not descended into the deep, nor yet into the underworld, nor have I ever ascended into heaven.'
Now, however, I have asked you only about fire and wind and the day through which you have passed, things from which you cannot be separated, and yet you have not answered me about them."
And he said to me: "You cannot understand the things that are your own, which have grown up with you;
how then can your vessel contain the way of the Most High? ... And how can one already worn out by a corrupt world understand incorruption?" And when I heard these things, I fell on my face
and said to him: "It would have been better for us not to be here than, having come into being, to live in ungodliness, and to suffer and not understand why."
And he answered me and said: "I went out to a forest of the trees of the plain, and they formed a plan
and said: 'Come, let us go and make war against the sea, so that it may recede before us, and let us make other forests for ourselves.'
And likewise the waves of the sea also formed a plan and said: 'Come, let us go up and subdue the forest of the plain, so that there also we may gain another region for ourselves.'
And the plan of the forest was in vain, for fire came and consumed it.
Likewise also was the plan of the waves of the sea, for the sand stood firm and stopped them.
If you were the judge of these, whom would you begin to justify or whom to condemn?"
And I answered and said: "Both formed a vain plan, for the land was given to the forest, and the sea has its place to bear its waves."
And he answered me and said: "You have judged well; why then have you not judged concerning yourself?

For just as the land is given to the forest and the sea to its waves, so also those who dwell upon the earth can understand only what is upon the earth, and those who are above the heavens only what is in the height of the heavens."
And I answered and said: "I implore you, my lord, why then was the capacity to understand given to me?

For I did not wish to ask about the ways above, but about the things that pass through us daily: why Israel has been given as a reproach to the gentiles; why the people whom you loved has been given over to godless tribes; why the law of our ancestors has been brought to ruin, and the written covenants are no more;
and why we pass from the world like locusts, and our life is like a mist, and we are not worthy to obtain mercy.
But what will he do for his name, which is invoked over us? Concerning these things I asked."
And he answered me and said: "If you survive you will see, and if you live you will marvel often, because the age is hurrying fast to pass away.
For it cannot bear what has been promised to the righteous in their seasons, because this age is full of sorrow and infirmities.
For the evil concerning which you ask me has been sown, but its harvest has not yet come.
If therefore that which has been sown is not reaped, and the place where the evil was sown does not depart, the field where the good is sown will not come.
For a grain of evil seed was sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, and how much ungodliness has it produced until now, and will produce until the threshing floor comes!
Consider now for yourself how much fruit of ungodliness a grain of evil seed has produced!
When ears of grain without number are sown, how great a threshing floor will they begin to fill!"
And I answered and said: "How and when will these things be? Why are our years few and evil?"
And he answered me and said: "Do not be in a greater hurry than the Most High; for you hasten on your own account, but the Most High on behalf of many."
Did not the souls of the righteous ask concerning these things in their chambers, saying, 'How long must I hope in this way? And when will come the fruit of the harvest of our reward?'
And Jeremiel the archangel answered them and said, 'When the number of those like you is fulfilled; for he has weighed the age in the balance,
and with a measure he has measured the times, and with a number he has numbered the times, and he will not move nor stir until the prescribed measure is fulfilled.'
Then I answered and said, 'O Sovereign Lord, but we also are all full of ungodliness.
And perhaps on our account the harvest of the righteous is withheld, because of the sins of those who inhabit the earth.'
And he answered me and said, 'Go and ask a pregnant woman whether, when she has fulfilled her nine months, her womb can still retain the offspring within itself.'
And I said, 'It cannot, lord.' And he said to me, 'In Hades the chambers of souls are made like the womb.
For just as a woman in labor hastens to escape the anguish of childbirth, so also these chambers hasten to give back the things that were entrusted to them
from the beginning. Then it will be shown to you concerning the things you desire to see.'
And I answered and said, 'If I have found favor in your sight, and if it is possible, and if I am capable,
show me this also: whether there is more to come than has already passed, or whether more has passed by us,
since I know what has passed, but what is to come I do not know.'
And he said to me, 'Stand on the right side, and I will show you the interpretation of the parable.'
So I stood and looked, and behold, a burning furnace passed before me; and it happened that when the flame had passed, I looked, and behold, smoke remained.
And after this, a cloud full of water passed before me and poured down a violent deluge of rain; and when the violent rush of rain had passed, drops remained in it.
And he said to me, 'Consider for yourself: just as the rain surpasses the drops, and the fire surpasses the smoke, so the measure that has passed has exceeded; but drops and smoke remain.'
And I prayed and said, 'Do you think I will live until those days? Or who will be alive in those days?'
He answered me and said, 'Concerning the signs about which you ask me, I can tell you in part; but concerning your life, I was not sent to tell you, for I do not know.'
'Now concerning the signs: Behold, the days will come when those who inhabit the earth will be seized with great panic, and the way of truth will be hidden, and the land will be barren of faith.
And unrighteousness will be multiplied beyond what you yourself now see and beyond what you heard of long ago.
And the land that you now see ruling will become trackless and untrodden, and they will see it desolate.
But if the Most High grants that you live, you will see it thrown into confusion after the third period, and the sun will suddenly shine forth by night and the moon by day.
And blood will drip from wood, and the stone will utter its voice, and the peoples will be perturbed,
and the courses of the stars will be altered. And one whom those who inhabit the earth do not expect will reign; and the birds will migrate together.
And the Sodomite Sea will cast up fish; and one whom many do not know will give voice by night, but all will hear its voice.
And chasms will appear in many places, and fire will frequently burst forth, and wild beasts will roam beyond their territory, and menstruous women will give birth to monsters;
and salt waters will be found in sweet waters. And all friends will war against one another; and then wisdom will be hidden, and understanding will withdraw into its chamber.
And it will be sought by many and not be found, and unrighteousness and unrestraint will be multiplied upon the earth.
And one region will ask its neighbor and say, "Has righteousness that makes a person righteous passed through you?" And it will deny it.
And it will happen at that time that people will hope and not obtain; they will labor, and their ways will not prosper.
These signs I am permitted to tell you; and if you pray again and weep as you do now, and fast for seven days, you will hear things even greater than these.'
Then I awoke, and my body trembled exceedingly, and my soul was so troubled that it grew faint.
And the angel who had come and was speaking with me took hold of me, and strengthened me, and set me upon my feet.
And it happened on the second night that Phaltiel, the leader of the people, came to me and said to me, 'Where were you, and why is your face sad?
Or do you not know that Israel has been entrusted to you in the land of their exile?'
Rise up therefore and eat some bread, and do not abandon us like a shepherd his flock in the hands of malicious wolves.
And I said to him, “Go away from me and do not come near me for seven days, and then you may come to me.” And he heard what I said and departed from me.
And I fasted seven days, wailing and weeping, just as the angel Uriel had commanded me.
And it came to pass after seven days that the thoughts of my heart were again very troublesome to me.
And my soul recovered the spirit of understanding, and again I began to speak words before the Most High,
and I said: “O Sovereign Lord, from all the forest of the earth and from all its trees you have chosen one vine;
and from all the lands of the world you have chosen for yourself one pit, and from all the flowers of the world you have chosen for yourself one lily;
and from all the deeps of the sea you have filled for yourself one stream, and from all the built cities you have sanctified Zion for yourself;
and from all created birds you have named for yourself one dove, and from all fashioned cattle you have provided for yourself one sheep;
and from all the multiplied peoples you have acquired for yourself one people, and to this people whom you desired you gave a law approved by all.
And now, O Lord, why have you handed over the one to the many, and set the one root above the others, and scattered your only one among the many?
And those who contradicted your promises have trampled down those who believed your covenants.
And if you truly hate your people, they ought to be punished by your own hands.”
And it came to pass, when I had spoken these words, that the angel who had previously come to me during the past night was sent to me,
and he said to me: “Listen to me, and I will instruct you; pay attention to me, and I will tell you more.”
And I said: “Speak, my lord.” And he said to me: “You are greatly distressed in mind concerning Israel. Do you love him more than he who made him?”
And I said: “No, lord, but out of grief have I spoken; for my innermost parts torment me every hour as I seek to grasp the path of the Most High and to search out a part of his judgment.”

And he said to me: “You cannot.” And I said: “Why, lord? Why was I born? Or why did not my mother’s womb become my grave, so that I might not see the travail of Jacob and the exhaustion of the people of Israel?”
And he said to me: “Number for me those who have not yet come, and gather for me the scattered drops, and make the withered flowers green again for me,
and open for me the closed chambers and bring out for me the winds shut up in them, or show me the likeness of a voice; and then I will show you the travail that you ask to see.”
And I said: “O Sovereign Lord, who is able to know these things, except one whose dwelling is not with human beings?
As for me, I am foolish; how then can I speak of these things about which you have asked me?”
And he said to me: “Just as you cannot do one of these things that have been mentioned, so you will not be able to find out my judgment or the ultimate love that I have promised for my people.”
And I said: “Yet behold, O Lord, you have charge over those who are alive at the end; but what will they do who were before us, or we, or those who come after us?”
And he said to me: “I will liken my judgment to a circle: just as there is no slowness of the last, so there is no swiftness of the first.”
And I answered and said: “Could you not have created all together—those who were made, those who are, and those who are to be—so that you might reveal your judgment more quickly?”
And he answered me and said: “The creation cannot run faster than the Creator, nor can the world sustain all together those who are created in it.”

And I said: “How is it that you said to your servant that you will give life all at once to the creation created by you? If therefore they will live all together and the creation will sustain them, it could even now bear those present all at once.”
And he said to me: “Ask the womb of a woman, and say to her: ‘If you bear ten children, why do you do so over time?’ Ask her therefore to bring forth ten all at once.”
And I said: “She certainly cannot, but only according to time.”
And he said to me: “So I too have given the womb of the earth to those who are sown upon it over time.
For just as an infant does not give birth, nor one who has grown old any longer, so have I arranged the world created by me.”
And I asked and said: “Since you have now opened the way for me, let me speak before you: Is our mother, of whom you spoke to me, still young, or is she now approaching old age?”
And he answered me and said: “Ask her who gives birth, and she will tell you.
For you shall say to her: ‘Why are those whom you have now borne not like those who were before, but smaller in stature?’
And she herself will say to you: 'Those who were born in the youth of strength are of one sort, and those born toward the time of old age, when the womb was failing, are of another.'
Consider therefore you also that you are smaller in stature than those who were before you,

and those who come after you will be smaller than you, as belonging to a creation already growing old and passing beyond the strength of youth. And I said: 'I beseech you, Lord, if I have found favor in your eyes, show your servant through whom you visit your creation.'
And he said to me: 'At the beginning of the terrestrial world, before the portals of the world stood, and before the gatherings of the winds blew,
and before the voices of the thunders sounded, and before the flashes of lightnings shone, and before the foundations of paradise were made firm,
and before the beautiful flowers were seen, and before the powers of the movements were established, and before the innumerable hosts of angels were gathered,
and before the heights of the air were lifted up, and before the measures of the firmaments were named, and before the footstool of Zion was weighed,
and before the present years were investigated, and before the schemes of those who now sin were alienated, and before those who have stored up faith were sealed—
then I planned these things, and they were made through me alone and not through another, just as the end also will come through me and not through another.'
And I answered and said: 'What will be the division of the times, or when will be the end of the first and the beginning of the following?'
And he said to me: 'From Abraham to Abraham, because Jacob and Esau were born from him; for Jacob's hand was holding Esau's heel from the beginning.
For Esau is the end of this age, and Jacob is the beginning of the one that follows.
For the end of a man is the heel, and the beginning of a man is the hand; between the heel and the hand seek nothing else, Ezra.'
And I answered and said: 'O Sovereign Lord, if I have found favor in your eyes,
show your servant the end of your signs, of which you showed me a part on the preceding night.'
And he answered and said to me: 'Stand up on your feet, and you will hear a voice full of sound.
And it will be that if the place on which you stand is violently shaken
while it speaks, do not be terrified, for the word is concerning the end. And the foundations of the earth will understand
that the speech is concerning them; it will tremble and be shaken, for it knows that their end must be transformed.'
And it came to pass when I had heard, I arose upon my feet and listened, and behold, a voice was speaking, and its sound was like the sound of many waters.
And it said: 'Behold, the days are coming, and it will be when I begin to draw near to visit those who dwell upon the earth,
and when I begin to require an account from those who have unrighteously harmed others by their injustice, and when the humiliation of Zion will be completed,
and when the age that is about to pass away is sealed, I will perform these signs: The books will be opened before the face of the firmament, and all will see together;
and one-year-old infants will speak with their voices, and pregnant women will give birth to premature infants of three and four months, and they will live and leap about;
and suddenly sown places will appear unsown, and full storehouses will suddenly be found empty;
and a trumpet will sound with a blast, which when all hear, they will suddenly be terrified.

And it will be at that time that friends will wage war against friends as enemies, and the earth will be terrified with those who dwell in it, and the veins of fountains will stand still so that they will not flow for three hours.
And it will be that whoever is left from all these things that I have foretold to you will be saved, and will see my salvation and the end of my age.
And the people who were taken up, who did not taste death from their birth, will be seen, and the heart of the earth's inhabitants will be changed and converted into a different mind.
For evil will be blotted out, and deceit will be extinguished.
Faith will flourish, corruption will be overcome, and the truth that was without fruit for so long a time will be revealed.'
And it came to pass while he was speaking to me, behold, little by little the place on which I was standing began to shake.
And he said to me: 'These things I have come to show you, both now and for the coming night.
If therefore you pray again and fast again for seven days, I will declare to you again greater things than these by day.
For your voice has surely been heard before the Most High; for the Mighty One has seen your uprightness and perceived the purity that you have maintained from your youth.'
And on this account he sent me to show you all these things, and to say to you: 'Have confidence, and do not fear,
and do not be hasty to ponder vain thoughts concerning former times, so that you may not be in haste regarding the last times.'
And it came to pass after this, that I wept again and fasted in like manner for seven days, in order to complete the three weeks that were appointed to me.
And it came to pass on the eighth night, that my heart was troubled within me once more, and I began to speak before the Most High.
For my spirit was greatly inflamed, and my soul was in distress.
And I said: 'O Lord, speaking you spoke from the beginning of creation on the first day, saying: "Let heaven and earth be made," and your word accomplished the work.
And at that time the spirit was hovering, and darkness was all around and silence; the sound of a human voice was not yet from you.
Then you commanded a ray of light to be brought forth from your treasuries, so that your works might then appear.
And on the second day you created the spirit of the firmament, and commanded it to divide and make a separation between the waters, so that one part moved upward and the other part remained below.

And on the third day you commanded the waters to be gathered together in the seventh part of the earth, but six parts you dried and preserved, so that from these, sown and cultivated, they might be of service before you.
For your word went forth, and immediately the work was done.

For suddenly there came forth an immense abundance of fruit, and manifold desires of taste, and flowers of inimitable color, and odors of unsearchable fragrance. And on the third day these things were made.
On the fourth day you commanded the splendor of the sun to be made, the light of the moon, and the arrangement of the stars,
and you commanded them to serve the human being who was to be formed.
On the fifth day you spoke to the seventh part where the water was gathered together, that it should bring forth living creatures, birds, and fish; and so it was done.
The mute and lifeless water brought forth living creatures as it was commanded, so that from this the nations might recount your wonders.
And then you preserved two living beings; the name of one you called Behemoth, and the name of the second you called Leviathan.
And you separated them from one another, for the seventh part where the water was gathered together could not contain them.
And you gave to Behemoth one part that was dried on the third day, to dwell in it, where there are a thousand mountains.
But to Leviathan you gave the watery seventh part; and you have kept them to be devoured by whom you will and when you will.
On the sixth day you commanded the earth to bring forth before you cattle and beasts and creeping things,
and over these, Adam, whom you made ruler over all the works that you created; and from him we are all derived, the people whom you have chosen.
All this I have spoken before you, O Lord, because you have said that for our sakes you created the firstborn world.
As for the other nations born of Adam, you have said that they are nothing, and that they are like spittle, and you have compared their abundance to a drop from a bucket.
And now, O Lord, behold, these nations, which are reputed as nothing, rule over us and devour us.
But we, your people, whom you have called your firstborn, your only-begotten, your zealous lover, your most beloved, are handed over into their hands.
And if the world was created for our sake, why do we not possess our world as an inheritance? How long shall these things be?'
And it came to pass when I had finished speaking these words, the angel who had been sent to me on the first nights was sent to me again,
and he said to me: 'Rise, Ezra, and hear the words that I have come to speak to you.'
And I said: 'Speak, my lord.' And he said to me: 'A sea is set in a wide expanse, so that it is deep and vast,
but its entrance is set in a narrow place, so that it is like a river.
For if anyone desires to enter the sea to behold it or to master it, how can he reach its expanse unless he passes through the narrow part?
Likewise another matter: A city is built and set upon a plain, and it is full of all good things,
but its entrance is narrow and set in a steep place, so that there is fire on the right hand, while on the left there is deep water.
And there is only one single path set between them, that is, between the fire and the water, so that the path can hold only one human footstep at a time.'
If now a city is given to a man as an inheritance, unless the heir passes through the danger set before it, how will he receive his inheritance?
And I said, "It is so, Lord." And he said to me, "So also is Israel's portion.
For on their account I made the world; and when Adam transgressed my statutes, what had been made was judged.
And the entrances of this world were made narrow, sorrowful, and toilsome, being few and evil, full of perils, and sustained by great hardships.
For the entrances of the greater world are spacious and secure, producing the fruit of immortality.
Therefore, unless the living enter into these narrow and futile conditions, they will not be able to receive the things that are laid up in store.
Now therefore, why are you disturbed, seeing that you are corruptible? And why are you troubled, since you are mortal?
And why have you not considered in your heart what is to come, but rather what is present?"
And I answered and said, "Sovereign Lord, behold, you have ordained in your law that the righteous shall inherit these things, but the ungodly shall perish.
The righteous, then, endure narrow things while hoping for the spacious; but those who have acted ungodly have both suffered narrowness and will not see the spacious."
And he said to me, "You are not a judge above God, nor do you possess understanding above the Most High.
For let many perish who are now present, rather than that the law of God set before them be disregarded.
For God strictly commanded those who came into the world when they arrived, what they should do to live, and what they should observe to avoid punishment.
Yet they were not persuaded and contradicted him; and they devised for themselves futile thoughts,
and proposed to themselves deceitful transgressions. They even declared that the Most High does not exist, and they did not acknowledge his ways.
They despised his law, rejected his covenants, placed no faith in his statutes, and did not perform his works.
Therefore, Ezra, empty things are for the empty, and full things are for the full.

For behold, the time will come, and it will be when the signs that I predicted to you arrive, that the bride will appear, the city will become visible, and the land that is now withdrawn will be revealed.
And everyone who is delivered from the aforesaid evils shall himself see my wonders.
For my Son Jesus will be revealed with those who are with him, and will bring joy to those who remain for four hundred years.
And it will be after these years that my Son Christ will die, along with all who possess human breath.
And the world will be turned back into the primeval silence for seven days, just as in the first beginnings, so that no one is left.
And after seven days the world, which is not yet awake, will be roused, and what is corruptible will die.
And the earth will give up those who sleep in it, and the dust those who dwell silently within it, and the storehouses will yield up the souls that were entrusted to them.
And the Most High will be revealed upon the seat of judgment, and mercies will pass away, and patience will be gathered up;
judgment alone will remain, truth will stand, and faithfulness will grow strong;
and recompense will follow, and the reward will be shown; deeds of righteousness will awake, and unrighteous deeds will not sleep.
And the pit of torment will appear, and opposite it will be the place of rest; the furnace of Gehenna will be displayed, and opposite it the paradise of delight.
And the Most High will then say to the resurrected nations: 'Look and understand whom you have denied, whom you have not served, and whose commandments you have despised.
Look on this side and on that: here is delight and rest, and there is fire and torments.' Thus he will speak to them on the day of judgment.
This day is of such a nature that it has neither sun nor moon nor stars,
nor cloud nor thunder nor lightning, nor wind nor water nor air, nor darkness nor evening nor morning,
nor summer nor spring nor heat, nor winter nor frost nor cold, nor hail nor rain nor dew,
nor noon nor night nor dawn, nor brightness nor clarity nor light, except only the splendor of the glory of the Most High, by which all will begin to see what has been set before them.
For it will have a duration of about a week of years."
This is my judgment and its prescription; but to you alone have I shown these things.
And I answered and said, 'I said then, O Lord, and I say now: Blessed are those who are present and observe what has been established by you.
But concerning those for whom my prayer was made: who among those present is there that has not sinned, or who among the born that has not transgressed your covenant?
And now I see that the coming age will bring delight to few, but torments to many.

For an evil heart has grown up in us, which has alienated us from these things and led us into corruption, and shown us the ways of death and the paths of destruction, and removed us far from life—and this not a few, but almost all who were created.'
And he answered me and said, 'Listen to me, and I will instruct you and correct you regarding what follows.
For this reason the Most High has made not one age, but two.
Because you said that the righteous are not many, but few, while the ungodly are multiplied, listen to this:
If you have very few precious stones, will you gather lead and clay to set them with, which abound?'
And I said, 'Lord, how can that be?'
And he said to me, 'Not only this, but ask the earth and it will tell you; flatter it and it will declare to you.
For you shall say to it: You produce gold and silver and bronze, and iron also, and lead and clay.
Now silver is more abundant than gold, and bronze than silver, and iron than bronze, lead than iron, and clay than lead.
Judge therefore for yourself which things are precious and desirable: that which is abundant, or that which is rare by nature?'
And I said, 'O Sovereign Lord, what is abundant is cheaper, for what is rarer is more precious.'
And he answered me and said, 'Weigh within yourself what you have thought, for he who has what is hard to get rejoices more than he who has an abundance.
So also is the creation promised by me. For I will rejoice over the few who will be saved, because it is they who have now made my glory prevail and through whom my name is now named.

And I will not grieve over the multitude of those who have perished, for they are the ones who are now likened to vapor, and are compared to flame and smoke; they have burned, boiled, and been extinguished.'
And I answered and said, 'O earth, what have you brought forth? If the mind is made from dust like the rest of creation,
then it would have been better if the dust itself had not been born, so that the mind might not have been formed from it.
For now understanding grows with us, and on account of this we are tormented, because we perish knowingly.
Let the human race mourn, and let the beasts of the field rejoice; let all who are born mourn, but let the four-footed beasts and the cattle be glad.
For it is much better for them than for us. For they do not expect a judgment, nor do they know of torments, nor is salvation promised to them after death.
For what does it profit us, that we shall be preserved, but shall be tormented with torment?
For all who have been born are entangled in iniquities, and full of sins, and burdened with transgressions.
And if we were not to come into judgment after death, perhaps it would have gone better with us.'
And he answered me and said, 'When the Most High was making the world and Adam and all who came from him, he first prepared the judgment and the things pertaining to the judgment.
And now understand from your own words, for you said that understanding grows with us.

Therefore, those who dwell on earth will be tormented for this reason: that having understanding they committed iniquity, and receiving commandments they did not keep them, and having obtained the law they violated what they received.
And what will they have to say in the judgment, or how will they answer in the last times?
For how long a time has the Most High shown patience toward those who inhabit the world—and not for their sake, but for the sake of the times that he foresaw!'

And I answered and said, 'If I have found favor before you, O Lord, show this also to your servant: whether after death, even now when each one of us surrenders his soul, we will be preserved in rest until those times come in which you begin to renew creation, or whether we will be tormented from now on?'
And he answered me and said, 'I will show you this also. But do not join yourself with those who have shown contempt, nor count yourself among those who are tormented.
For you have a treasure of works laid up with the Most High, but it will not be shown to you until the last times.

Now concerning death, the teaching is: When the final sentence has gone out from the Most High that a human should die, as the breath departs from the body to return again to him who gave it, it first of all adores the glory of the Most High.
And if indeed it is of those who scorned and did not keep the way of the Most High, and of those who despised his law, and of those who hated those who fear God,
these spirits will not enter into habitations, but from now on will wander in torments, grieving always and sorrowful, in seven ways.
The first way, because they have scorned the law of the Most High.
The second way, because they can no longer make a good return, that they may live.
The third way, they see the reward stored up for those who have believed the covenants of the Most High.
The fourth way, they will consider the torment stored up for themselves in the last times.
The fifth way, they see the habitations of the others guarded by angels with great silence.
The sixth way, they see how torment will pass over upon them.

The seventh way, which is greater than all the aforesaid ways, because they will waste away in confusion, and be consumed in dishonor, and wither in fears, seeing the glory of the Most High before whom they sinned while living, and before whom they will begin to be judged in the last times.
Now this is the order of those who have kept the ways of the Most High, when they begin to be separated from the corruptible vessel.
During the time they dwelt in it, they served the Most High with labor, and endured danger at every hour, so that they might guard the law of the Lawgiver perfectly.
Therefore, this is the word concerning them:
First of all, they see with great joy the glory of him who receives them, for they shall rest in seven orders.
The first order, because they have struggled with much labor to overcome the evil thought formed with them, that it might not seduce them from life to death.
The second order, because they see the confusion in which the souls of the ungodly wander, and the punishment that awaits them.
The third order, seeing the testimony that he who formed them testified concerning them, that while living they kept the law that was given through faith.
The fourth order, understanding the rest which, now gathered in their storehouses, they enjoy in great silence guarded by angels, and the glory that awaits them in their last times.

The fifth order, exulting how they have now escaped what is corruptible, and how in the future they will possess an inheritance, seeing also the narrow and toil-filled state from which they have now been set free, and beginning to receive the spacious room, enjoying it and immortal.
The sixth order, when it is shown to them how their face will begin to shine like the sun, and how they will begin to be made like the light of the stars, no longer corruptible from now on.

The seventh order, which is greater than all the aforesaid, because they will exult with boldness, and because they will be confident without being confused, and will rejoice without fear; for they hasten to see the face of him whom they served while living, and from whom they begin to receive their reward in glory.
This is the order of the souls of the righteous, as is announced henceforth; and the aforesaid ways are the torments which those who have been negligent suffer henceforth.
And I answered and said, "Will time therefore be given to souls, after they are separated from the bodies, to see what you have told me?"
And he said to me, "Their freedom will be for seven days, so that during the seven days they may see the things that have been foretold, and afterwards they will be gathered in their habitations."

And I answered and said, "If I have found favor before your eyes, show yet to me, your servant, whether on the day of judgment the righteous will be able to intercede for the ungodly or plead with the Most High for them,"
"whether fathers for sons or sons for parents, whether brothers for brothers, whether relatives for kinsmen, whether friends for their most beloved."

And he answered me and said, "Because you have found favor before my eyes, I will show this also to you. The day of judgment is decisive, displaying to all the seal of truth. Just as now a father does not send a son, or a son a father, or a master a servant, or a trusted friend his most beloved, that he might understand or sleep or eat or be healed in his place,"
"so no one will ever pray for another; for everyone will then bear each his own unrighteousness or righteousness."
And I answered and said, "Then how do we find now that Abraham first prayed on behalf of the people of Sodom, and Moses for the fathers who sinned in the wilderness,"
"and Joshua who came after him for Israel in the days of Achan, and Samuel in the days of Saul,"
"and David for the plague, and Solomon for those in the sanctuary,"
"and Elijah for those who received rain, and for the dead that he might live,"
"and Hezekiah for the people in the days of Sennacherib, and many for many?"
"If therefore now, when corruptibility has increased and unrighteousness has multiplied, the righteous have prayed for the ungodly, why will it not be so then also?"
And he answered me and said, "The present age is not the end; glory does not abide in it frequently; therefore those who were able prayed for the weak."
"For the day of judgment will be the end of this time and the beginning of the immortal time to come, in which corruption has passed away,"
intemperance is dissolved, unbelief is cut off, but righteousness has grown, and truth has arisen.
Therefore, at that time no one will be able to have mercy on him who has been defeated in judgment, nor to harm him who has conquered.
And I answered and said: This is my first and last word, that it would have been better not to give the earth to Adam, or, when he had given it, to restrain him so that he would not sin.
For what does it profit all people in the present to live in grief, and when dead to expect punishment?
O Adam, what have you done? For though it was you who sinned, the fall was not yours alone, but also ours who come from you.
For what does it profit us that an immortal time has been promised to us, whereas we have done deeds of death?
And that an everlasting hope has been predicted for us, whereas we have become utterly futile?
And that dwellings of health and safety are reserved, whereas we have lived evilly?
And that the glory of the Most High will protect those who have lived purely, whereas we have walked in the worst of ways?
And that paradise will be revealed, whose fruit remains incorruptible, in which is abundance and healing,
yet we shall not enter it, for we have lived in unseemly places?
And that the faces of those who practiced self-restraint will shine above the stars, whereas our faces will be blacker than darkness?
For while living we did not consider, when we were committing iniquity, what we would begin to suffer after death.
And he answered and said: This is the meaning of the contest which the human being born upon the earth has fought:
that if he is defeated he shall suffer what you have said, but if he conquers he shall receive what I say.
For this is the way of which Moses spoke while he lived, saying to the people: 'Choose life for yourself, so that you may live.'
Yet they did not believe him, nor the prophets after him, nor even me who have spoken to them,
so that there should be no sorrow over their destruction, even as there will be joy over those for whom salvation is assured.
And I answered and said: I know, Lord, that the Most High is now called merciful, in that he has mercy on those who have not yet come into the world,
and compassionate, in that he has compassion on those who turn to his law,
and patient, because he shows patience to those who have sinned, as his own works,
and bountiful, because he prefers to give rather than to demand,
and of great mercy, because he multiplies his mercies more and more to those who are present, and to those who have passed away, and to those who are to come.
For if he did not multiply them, the world would not remain alive with those who inhabit it.

And a giver, because if he did not give out of his goodness, so that those who have committed iniquities might be relieved of their iniquities, not even the ten-thousandth part of humanity could be kept alive;
and a judge, for if he did not pardon those who were created by his word and blot out the multitude of their contempts, of the innumerable multitude there would perhaps be left only very few.
And he answered me and said: The Most High made this age for the sake of many, but the age to come for the sake of few.

Now I will tell a parable before you, Ezra. Just as you might ask the earth and it will tell you that it yields much more clay from which pottery is made, but only a little dust from which gold comes, so also is the course of the present age.
Many indeed have been created, but few will be saved.
And I answered and said: Let the soul, then, drink in understanding and devour what is wise!
For you came without your consent and departed unwillingly, and no time was given to you except only to live for a short while.

O Lord over us, if you will permit your servant that we may pray before you, give us seed for the heart and cultivation for the mind whence fruit may come, by which every corruptible one who bears the likeness of a human being may be able to live.
For you alone exist, and we are one fashioned work of your hands, just as you have spoken.

And because you now give life to the body fashioned in the womb and supply its members, your creation is preserved in fire and water, and for nine months your fashioned work endures your creature that was created in it.
Yet that which preserves and that which is preserved will both be preserved by your preservation. And when the womb again delivers what has grown in it,
you commanded that from the members themselves, that is, the breasts, milk should be provided, the fruit of the breasts,
so that what has been formed might be nourished for a certain time; and afterwards you direct him according to your mercy,
you nourished him in your righteousness, and instructed him in your law, and disciplined him in your understanding,
and you will put him to death as your creation, and make him alive as your work.
If therefore you will lightly destroy him who was formed with such great labors at your command, why then was he made?
And now I will speak: Concerning humanity in general you know best, but concerning your people, on whose account I grieve,
and concerning your inheritance, on whose account I mourn, and concerning Israel, on whose account I am sorrowful, and concerning the seed of Jacob, on whose account I am troubled.
Therefore I will begin to pray before you for myself and for them, because I see the failings of us who inhabit the earth,
for I have heard of the swiftness of the judgment that is to come.
Therefore hear my voice and understand my words, and I will speak before you.
The beginning of the words of Ezra before he was taken up. And he said: “O Lord, who dwell forever, whose eyes are exalted and whose upper chambers are in the air,
and whose throne is beyond estimate and whose glory is incomprehensible, before whom the host of angels stands with trembling,
whose service is turned into wind and fire, whose word is true and whose utterances endure,
whose command is strong and whose ordinance is terrible, whose look dries up the abysses, and whose indignation makes the mountains melt away, and whose truth bears witness:
Hear, O Lord, the prayer of your servant, and give ear to the petition of your creature; attend to my words.
For as long as I live I will speak, and as long as I have understanding I will answer.
Do not look upon the sins of your people, but upon those who serve you in truth.
Do not regard the pursuits of those who act wickedly, but of those who have kept your testimonies amid sorrows.
Do not think of those who have lived deceitfully in your sight, but remember those who willingly have known your fear.
Do not choose to destroy those who lived like cattle, but look upon those who have gloriously taught your law.
Do not be indignant with those who are deemed worse than beasts, but love those who have always trusted in your glory.
For we and our fathers have lived by mortal ways, but on account of us sinners you will be called merciful.
For if you desire to have mercy on us, then you will be called merciful, since we have no works of righteousness.
For the righteous, who have many works stored up with you, will receive their reward on the basis of their own works.
For what is man, that you should be angry with him? Or what is a corruptible race, that you should be so bitter toward it?
For in truth there is no one among those born who has not acted wickedly, and among those who profess you, none who has not transgressed.
For in this your righteousness and your goodness will be declared, O Lord, when you have mercy on those who have no store of good works.”
And he answered me and said: “You have spoken some things rightly, and according to your words so it shall be.
For indeed I will not think upon the creation of those who have sinned, or their death, or their judgment, or their destruction;
but I will rejoice over the creation of the righteous, their pilgrimage also, and their salvation, and their receipt of reward.
As I have spoken, therefore, so it is.

For just as a farmer sows many seeds upon the ground and plants a multitude of seedlings, yet in time not all that were sown are preserved, nor do all that were planted take root, so also those who have been sown in the world will not all be saved.”
Then I answered and said: “If I have found favor, let me speak,
for if the seed of the farmer does not come up—because it did not receive your rain in due season—or if it is ruined by too much rain,

it perishes; but man, who has been formed by your hands and is called your own image, because he is made in the likeness of the one for whose sake you formed all things—have you really compared him to the seed of the farmer?”
Not over us, but spare your people and have mercy on your inheritance; for you have mercy on your own creation.
And he answered me and said: "The things that are present are for those who are present, and the things that are future are for those who are future.
For you come far short of being able to love my creation more than I do. But you have often brought yourself near to the unrighteous; never do so!
Yet in this also you will be praiseworthy before the Most High,
because you have humbled yourself, as is fitting for you, and have not counted yourself among the righteous. You will be greatly glorified,
because many miserable afflictions will affect those who inhabit the world in the last times, because they have walked in great pride.
But as for you, understand for yourself, and seek out glory for those who are like you.

For to you paradise is opened, the tree of life is planted, the future age is prepared, abundance is made ready, a city is built, rest is approved, goodness is perfected, and wisdom is perfected beforehand.
The root is sealed off from you, infirmity is extinguished from you, and death is hidden; Hades has fled, and corruption has gone into oblivion.
Sorrows have passed away, and at the end the treasure of immortality is revealed.
Therefore, do not ask any further questions concerning the multitude of those who perish.
For they also, having received freedom, despised the Most High, showed contempt for his law, and abandoned his ways.
Moreover, they even trampled down his righteous ones,
and said in their heart that there is no God, even though they knew that they must die.
For just as the things predicted will receive you, so the thirst and torment that are prepared will receive them. For the Most High did not intend for humanity to be destroyed,
but those who were created have themselves defiled the name of him who made them, and were ungrateful to him who prepared life for them now.
Therefore my judgment is now drawing near,
which I have not shown to all, but only to you and to a few like you." And I answered and said:
"Behold now, Lord, you have shown me the multitude of the signs that you will begin to perform in the last times, but you have not shown me at what time."
The beginning of the words of the prayer of Ezra before he was taken up. He said: "O Lord, who inhabit eternity, whose are the highest heavens and whose upper chambers are in the air,
whose throne is beyond estimate and whose glory is incomprehensible, before whom the heavenly hosts stand with trembling,
and at whose word they are changed into wind and fire; whose word is true and whose speech endures,
whose command is most mighty and whose ordinance is awesome, whose look dries up the abysses and whose rebuke makes the mountains melt away, and whose truth is attested.
Hear the voice of your servant, give heed to the supplication of your fashioned creature, and attend to my words.
For while I still live I will speak, and while I still have understanding I will answer.
Do not look upon the sins of your people, but upon those who have served you in truth.
Do not regard those who act wickedly in their sins, but those who have kept your covenants amid torments.
Do not think about those who have lived perversely before you, but about those who willingly resolved to know the fear of you.
Do not desire to destroy those who have lived like beasts, but look upon those who have clearly displayed your glorious law.
Do not be angry with those who are judged worse than beasts, but love those who have continually hoped in your glory.
For we and those before us have walked in corrupt ways; but because of us who have sinned, you are called merciful.
For if you desire to have mercy on us who have no good works, then you will be called merciful,
since the righteous, who have many works stored up with you, receive their reward on the basis of their own deeds.
For what is mortal man that you should be angry with him, or a corrupt race that you should be indignant with them?
For in truth there is no one among those who are born who has not done wickedly, nor any among those who have grown up who has not sinned."
For in this your goodness, O Lord, will be made manifest, when you have mercy on those who have no store of good works.
He answered me and said: “Measure carefully within yourself; and when you see that a certain part of the predicted signs has passed,
then you will understand that it is the very time in which the Most High is about to visit the world that was made by him.
And when there shall be seen in the world earthquakes of places, tumult of peoples, plottings of nations, instability of leaders, and confusion of princes,
then you will understand that of these things the Most High spoke from the days that were of old, from the beginning.
For just as with everything that is made in the world, the beginning leads to the end and the end is made manifest,
so also are the times of the Most High: the beginnings are manifest in wonders and mighty works, and the consummation in deeds and signs.
And it shall be that everyone who is saved and who is able to escape by his works or by the faith in which he has believed,
shall survive the predicted dangers and shall see my salvation in my land and within my borders, which I have sanctified for myself from eternity.
Then those who have now abused my ways will be astonished, and those who have cast them away in contempt shall dwell in torments.
For as many as did not acknowledge me in their lifetime, though they received benefits,
and as many as scorned my law while they still possessed freedom,
and when the opportunity for repentance was still open to them did not understand, but despised it, these must know it after death in torment.
Therefore, do not be curious any longer about how the ungodly will be tormented, but inquire how the righteous will be saved, whose world it is, and for whose sake the world was made, and when.”
I answered and said:
“I have said before, and I say now, and I will say hereafter, that there are more who perish than who will be saved,
as a wave exceeds a drop.” And he answered me and said:

“As the field is, so also are the seeds; and as the flowers are, so are the dyes; and as the work is, so is the creation; and as the farmer is, so is the threshing floor. For there was a time of the world,
and then, when I was preparing for those who exist now, before the world in which they should dwell was made for them, no one opposed me
then, for no one existed; but now, having been created in this world that was prepared, with a never-failing table and an unsearchable law, they have become corrupt in their ways.
So I considered my world, and behold, it was lost; and my earth, and behold, it was in peril because of the devices that had come into it.
And I saw and spared them with great difficulty, and saved for myself a grape out of a cluster, and a plant out of a great forest.
Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain, and let my grape and my plant be preserved, because with much labor I have perfected them.
But you, if you will wait yet seven more days—though you shall not fast during them—
shall go into a field of flowers where no house has been built, and eat only of the flowers of the field; you shall taste no meat and drink no wine, but eat only flowers,
and pray to the Most High without ceasing, and I will come and speak with you.”
So I went, as he told me, into the field called Ardat; and there I sat among the flowers and ate of the herbs of the field, and their food satisfied me.
And it came to pass after seven days that I was lying on the grass, and my heart was troubled again, just as before.
And my mouth was opened, and I began to speak before the Most High, and said:
“O Lord, showing yourself among us, you were shown to our ancestors in the wilderness, when they came out of Egypt and when they entered the untrodden and unfruitful desert, and you spoke, saying:
‘Hear me, O Israel, and give heed to my words, O seed of Jacob.
For behold, I sow my law in you, and it shall bring forth fruit in you, and you shall be glorified in it forever.’
Yet our ancestors, though they received the law, did not keep it and did not observe my statutes. And it came to pass that the fruit of the law did not perish—for it could not, because it was yours—
yet those who received it perished, because they did not keep what had been sown in them.
And behold, it is the custom that when the ground has received seed, or the sea a ship, or any other vessel food or drink, and when it happens that it is destroyed,
that which was sown, or what was sent, or the things that were received, these are destroyed, while the container remains. But with us it has not happened in this way.
For we who received the law, having sinned, shall perish, along with our heart that received it;
yet the law does not perish, but abides in its glory.

While I was saying these things in my heart, I looked with my eyes and saw a woman on the right side; and behold, she was mourning and weeping with a loud voice, and was grieving deeply in soul; her clothes were torn, and ashes were upon her head.
Then I dismissed the thoughts that I had been pondering, and turned to her and said to her:
“Why are you weeping, and why are you grieving in soul?” And she said to me:
“Leave me alone, my lord, so that I may weep for myself and increase my sorrow, for I am very bitter in soul and brought very low.”
And I said to her, “What has happened to you? Tell me.” And she said to me:
“I, your maidservant, was barren and bore no child, though I had a husband for thirty years.
For during these thirty years, every hour and every day, night and day, I made supplication to the Most High.

And it came to pass after thirty years that God heard me, your handmaid, and looked upon my low estate, and considered my distress, and gave me a son. And I rejoiced greatly over him, both I and my husband and all my fellow citizens, and we gave great honor to the Mighty One.
And I brought him up with great labor.
And it came to pass, when he was grown and I had come to take a wife for him, that I made a feast day.
And it came to pass that when my son entered his wedding chamber, he fell down and died.
Then we all put out the lamps, and all my fellow citizens arose to comfort me; and I remained quiet until the next day, even until night.
And it came to pass, when they had all ceased comforting me so that I might rest, that I arose by night and fled, and came, as you see, into this field.
And I intend now not to return to the city, but to remain here, neither eating nor drinking, but mourning and fasting without ceasing until I die.”
Then I broke off the thoughts in which I was engaged, and answered her with anger, saying:
“You most foolish of all women! Do you not see our mourning, and what has happened to us?
For Zion, the mother of us all, is sorrowing with great grief and brought down in deep humiliation. Mourn most bitterly,
and now because we are all mourning, be sorrowful, since we all are grieving; yet you grieve for one son.
For ask the earth, and she will tell you that it is she who ought to mourn, being the survivor of so many that have sprouted upon her.
And from her all were born from the beginning, and others shall come; and behold, almost all go to destruction, and a multitude of them come to ruin.
Who then ought to mourn more—she who has lost so great a multitude, or you who grieve for one? But if you say to me,
‘My lamentation is not like that of the earth, for I have lost the fruit of my womb, which I bore with sorrows and brought forth with pains;
while the earth, according to the way of the earth, the present multitude in it has departed just as it came’—then I say to you:
Just as you bore with sorrow, so also the earth has from the beginning yielded her fruit, humanity, to the One who made her.
Now therefore keep your sorrow to yourself, and bear courageously the misfortunes that have befallen you.
For if you acknowledge the decree of God to be just, you will both receive your son back in due time and be praised among women.
Go, therefore, into the city to your husband.” And she said to me:
“I will not do so, nor will I enter the city, but here I will die.”
And I proceeded to speak to her again, and said:
“Do not speak in this way, but allow yourself to be persuaded—for what are the misfortunes of Zion?—and be comforted because of the sorrow of Jerusalem.
For you see that our sanctuary has been laid waste, our altar demolished, our temple destroyed,

and our harp is brought low, our hymn is silenced, our jubilation is ended, the light of our lampstand is extinguished, the ark of our covenant is plundered, our holy things are defiled, and the name that was invoked over us is almost profaned; our freeborn children have suffered dishonor, our priests are burned, our Levites have gone into captivity, our virgins are defiled, our wives have been violated, our righteous are seized, our little ones surrendered, our young men enslaved, and our strong men made powerless.”
And what is greatest of all, the seal of Zion—for she has now been stripped of her glory and handed over into the hands of those who hate us.
Therefore shake off your great sorrow and put aside the multitude of your griefs, so that the Mighty One may be reconciled to you and the Most High may grant you rest, a relief from your labors.

And it came to pass while I was speaking to her, behold, her face suddenly shone exceedingly, and her countenance took on the appearance of lightning, so that I was terrified of her and wondered what this might be.
And behold, suddenly she uttered a loud cry full of terror, so that the earth shook at the sound. And I looked,
and behold, the woman appeared to me no longer, but a city was being built, and a place was revealed with massive foundations. And I was afraid, and cried out with a loud voice, saying:
Where is the angel Uriel, who came to me at first? For it was he who caused me to fall into the multitude of this trance; and my end has turned to corruption, and my prayer to reproach.
And while I was saying these things, behold, the angel who had come to me at first came to me, and he saw me;
and behold, I lay there like a dead man and my understanding was alienated. Then he took hold of my right hand, strengthened me, set me on my feet, and said to me:
What is the matter with you? Why are you troubled, and why are your understanding and the thoughts of your heart perturbed? And I said:
Because you have utterly abandoned me! Yet I did according to your words and went out into the field, and behold, I have seen and still see what I am unable to describe. And he said to me:
Stand up like a man, and I will instruct you. And I said:
Speak, my lord; only do not abandon me, lest I die in vain,
for I have seen what I did not know, and I hear what I do not understand.
Or is my mind deceived and my soul dreaming?
Now therefore I beseech you to explain this vision to your servant. And he answered me and said:
Listen to me, and I will teach you and tell you about the things you fear; for the Most High has revealed many mysteries to you.
He has seen your righteous path, that you have unceasingly grieved for your people and mourned greatly over Zion.
This, then, is the meaning of the vision: The woman who appeared to you a little while ago,
whom you saw mourning and began to comfort,
now, however, you no longer see the likeness of a woman, but a city being built has appeared to you.
And as for her telling you about the misfortune of her son, this is the interpretation:
This woman whom you saw is Zion, whom you now behold as an established city.
And as for her saying to you that she was barren for thirty years, it is because there were three thousand years in the world when no offering was yet offered in her.
And it came to pass after those years that Solomon built the city and offered sacrifices; that was when the barren woman bore a son.
And as for her telling you, 'I reared him with labor,' this was the dwelling in Jerusalem.
And as for her saying to you that 'my son entered his bridal chamber and died, and misfortune befell him,' this was the destruction that overtook Jerusalem.
And behold, you saw her likeness, how she mourned her son, and you began to comfort her for what had happened; these things were to be disclosed to you.
And now, seeing that you are sincerely grieved and suffer with your whole heart on her account, the Most High has shown you the brilliance of her glory and the beauty of her splendor.
For this reason I told you to remain in the field where no house had been built.
For I knew that the Most High was about to show you these things.
Therefore I told you to go into the field where there is no foundation of any building.
For no work of human building could stand in the place where the city of the Most High was about to be revealed.
Therefore do not fear, and do not let your heart be dismayed, but enter and see the splendor and the greatness of the building, as far as your eyes are capable of seeing.
And after this you will hear as much as your ears are capable of hearing.
For you are blessed beyond many, and are named before the Most High as only a few are.
Now on the night that will follow tomorrow, you shall remain here,
and the Most High will show you those dream visions which the Most High will bring upon those who dwell on the earth in the last days.
So I slept that night and the next, just as he had told me.
And it came to pass on the second night that I saw a dream, and behold, there rose up from the sea an eagle that had twelve feathered wings and three heads.
And I looked, and behold, it spread its wings over all the earth, and all the winds of heaven blew upon it, and the clouds were gathered to it.
And I looked, and out of its wings grew opposing wings, and they became small and tiny pinions.
For its heads were at rest, and the middle head was larger than the other heads, but it too was resting with them.
And I looked, and behold, the eagle flew on its wings and reigned over the earth and over those who dwell in it.
And I saw how all things under heaven were subjected to it, and no one spoke against it, not even a single one of the creatures on the earth.
And I looked, and behold, the eagle rose upon its claws and uttered a voice to its wings, saying:
“Do not all watch at the same time; let each sleep in its place and watch in turn,
but let the heads be preserved for the end.”
And I looked, and behold, the voice did not go out from its heads, but from the midst of its body.
And I numbered its opposing wings, and behold, there were eight of them.
And I looked, and behold, on the right side one wing arose and reigned over all the earth.
And it came to pass while it was reigning that its end came, and it disappeared, so that even its place was no longer seen. And the next arose and reigned, and it held power for a long time.
And it came to pass while it was reigning that its end also came, so that it disappeared like the first.
And behold, a voice went out to it, saying:
“Hear, you who have held the earth for so long a time, this I announce to you before you begin to disappear:
No one after you shall hold your time, nor even the half of it.”
And the third raised itself up and held the rule like the former ones, and it also disappeared.
And so it happened to all the wings, to exercise rule one by one and then to appear nowhere again.

And I looked, and behold, in time the succeeding wings on the right side were also raised up, so that they too might hold the rule; and there were some of them that held it, but nevertheless disappeared immediately.
For some of them were raised up, but did not hold the rule.
And after this I looked, and behold, the twelve wings and two little wings disappeared.
And nothing remained on the body of the eagle except three resting heads and six little wings.
And I looked, and behold, of the six little wings two were separated and remained under the head that was on the right side; for four remained in their place.
And I looked, and behold, these underwings were planning to raise themselves up and to hold the rule.
And I looked, and behold, one was raised up, but immediately disappeared.
And a second, and this one disappeared even more quickly than the first.
And I looked, and behold, the two that remained planned within themselves to reign also.
And while they were planning, behold, one of the resting heads, which was the middle one, awoke; for this was larger than the other two heads.
And I saw how it joined the two heads with itself,
and behold, the head turned with those that were with it and devoured the two underwings that were planning to reign.
Moreover, this head held sway over all the earth and dominated those who dwell in it with great oppression, and it held power over the world above all the wings that had been.
And after this I looked, and behold, the middle head suddenly disappeared, and this just like the wings.
Moreover, two heads remained, which themselves also ruled over the earth and over those who inhabit it in like manner.
And I looked, and behold, the head on the right side devoured the one that was on the left.
And I heard a voice saying to me: “Look opposite you and consider what you see.”
And I looked, and behold, as it were a lion roused out of the forest, roaring; and I heard how it uttered a human voice to the eagle and spoke, saying:
“Listen, you, and I will speak to you; and the Most High says to you:
‘Are you not the one that remains of the four beasts that I made to reign in my world, that through them the end of my times might come?’

And you, the fourth, coming, have conquered all the beasts that have passed away, and holding sway over the world with great terror and over the whole earth with grievous oppression, and they inhabited the whole earth for so long a time with deceit.
And you have judged the earth not with truth.

For you have afflicted the meek and injured the peaceful; you have hated those who speak the truth and loved liars; and you have destroyed the dwellings of those who bore fruit, and cast down the walls of those who did you no harm.
And your insolence has ascended to the Most High, and your pride to the Mighty One.
And the Most High has looked upon his times, and behold, they are ended, and his ages are completed.
Therefore, you will surely disappear, you eagle, and your terrifying wings, and your wicked little wings, and your malicious heads, and your malicious talons, and your whole worthless body,
so that all the earth may be refreshed and relieved, freed from your violence, and hope for the judgment and mercy of him who made it.”
And it happened, while the lion was speaking these words to the eagle, that I looked,
and behold, the head that had remained disappeared; and the two wings that crossed over to it were set up to reign, and their reign was frail and full of turmoil.

And I looked, and behold, they did not appear, and the entire body of the eagle was burned, and the earth was exceedingly terrified. And I awoke from great bewilderment of mind and from great fear, and I said to my spirit:
“Behold, you have brought these things upon me, in that you search out the ways of the Most High.
Behold, I am still weary in my mind and very weak in my spirit, and there is not even a little strength in me from the great fear with which I was terrified this night.
Now therefore I will pray to the Most High, that he may strengthen me to the end.”
And I said: “O Sovereign Lord, if I have found favor before your eyes, and if I am accounted righteous before you beyond many, and if my prayer has truly ascended before your face,
strengthen me and show to me, your servant, the interpretation and distinction of this terrifying vision, that you may fully comfort my soul.
For you have judged me worthy to show me the end of times and the last things of the times.” And he said to me:
“This is the interpretation of this vision that you saw:
The eagle that you saw coming up from the sea, this is the fourth kingdom that appeared in a vision to Daniel your brother,
but it was not interpreted to him as I now interpret it to you or have interpreted it.
Behold, the days are coming when a kingdom shall arise upon the earth, and it shall be more terrifying than all the kingdoms that were before it.
And twelve kings shall reign in it, one after another.
For the second who shall begin to reign will himself hold power for a longer time than any of the twelve.
This is the interpretation of the twelve wings that you saw.
And as for your hearing a voice speaking that did not come out from its heads, but from the midst of its body,

this is the interpretation: that after the time of that kingdom no small contentions shall arise, and it shall be in danger of falling; yet it shall not fall then, but shall be established again to its beginning.
And as for your seeing the eight under-wings clinging to its wings,
this is the interpretation: For eight kings shall arise in it, whose times shall be short and their years swift; and two of them indeed shall perish
when the middle time draws near; but four shall be kept for the time when its time begins to draw near to its end, while two shall be kept for the end.”
And as for the three heads you saw resting,
this is the interpretation: In its last days the Most High will raise up three kingdoms and will renew many things in them, and they will rule over the earth
and over those who inhabit it, with great oppression beyond all who were before them. Therefore they are called the heads of the eagle.
For it is they who will sum up its wicked deeds and who will bring to an end its last days.
And as for your seeing the larger head disappear, it is because one of them will die upon his bed, and yet in torment.
For as for the two that remained, the sword will devour them.
For the sword of the one will devour the one who is with him, yet he too will fall by the sword in the last days.
And as for your seeing two underwings passing over to the head that is on the right side,
this is the interpretation: These are those whom the Most High has kept for his end; this was a small kingdom and full of trouble,
just as you saw. And as for the lion whom you saw roused from the forest, roaring and speaking to the eagle and reproving it for its unrighteousness through all its words, as you heard,
this is the Messiah, whom the Most High has kept until the end against them and their wicked deeds. He will reprove them for their unrighteousness and will confront them with their contempt.
For he will first set them alive before judgment, and when he has reproved them, then he will destroy them.

For he will deliver the rest of my people with mercy, those who have been preserved throughout my borders, and he will make them joyful until the end comes, the day of judgment, concerning which I spoke to you from the beginning.
This is the dream that you saw, and this is its interpretation.
You alone, therefore, were worthy to know this secret of the Most High.
Therefore write in a book all these things that you have seen, and put them in a hidden place.
And you shall teach them to the wise among your people, whose hearts you know are able to comprehend and keep these secrets.
As for you, wait here another seven days, so that whatever it pleases the Most High to show you may be shown to you."

And he departed from me. And it came to pass, when all the people heard that the seven days had passed and I had not returned to the city, they all gathered together, from the least to the greatest, and came to me, and spoke to me, saying:
"What sin have we committed against you, and what wrong have we done to you, that you have forsaken us and sat in this place?
For you alone among all the prophets are left to us, like a cluster of grapes from the vintage, and like a lamp in a dark place, and like a harbor for a ship saved from a storm.
Are not the evils that have befallen us enough?
If you forsake us, how much better it would have been for us if we too had been consumed in the burning of Zion!
